questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The War of the Spanish Succession and its effect on trade
The South Sea Company and its stock bubble and collapse
The Bank of England's rise as Britain's central bank
British slave law and the abolition of the Asiento trade
questions.explain: It describes the company's founding, its stock bubble in 1720 and the collapse.

questions.q: What monopoly was granted to the company in 1713?
options: The Asiento de Plata to mine silver in Spanish Peru
The Asiento de Vino to ship Spanish wine into Britain
The Asiento de Negros to supply enslaved Africans
The Asiento de Té to import tea from East India ports
questions.explain: It got the Asiento de Negros monopoly.

questions.q: What did the Bubble Act 1720 forbid?
options: Trading in enslaved Africans without a royal licence
Creating joint-stock companies without a royal charter
Insider trading by directors of public companies
Issuing government debt without parliamentary approval
questions.explain: It forbade joint-stock companies without royal charter, promoted by the company itself.

questions.q: What happened to those found to have profited unlawfully?
options: They were imprisoned in the Tower of London for years
Their assets were confiscated in proportion to their gains
They were exiled to the colonies and stripped of titles
They were fined a flat sum paid to the Bank of England
questions.explain: Personal assets were confiscated proportionate to their gains.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the share price?
options: It reflected strong profits from South American trade
It was driven by hype rather than actual trade profits
It was set by Parliament
It was stable
questions.explain: Expectations of profits were talked up and bubble prices exceeded what the business could justify.
